title.tagline: The sky only warns you once.
title.season_sub: Eight chase days, April to June
title.free_sub: Alone, two on one screen, or against a rival crew
title.online_sub: A crew of two, or the race for the best shots

d1.name: First day
d1.desc: One isolated cell, just enough shear. Eli says “marginal”; June says “perfect to shake off the rust”. A clean shot of the structure, maybe a shy tornado.

d2.name: Two cells
d2.desc: Two storms two hours apart. Pick the right one, then switch targets without getting stuck in the mud.

d3.name: The cowboy
d3.desc: Dutch Callahan and his crew are on the same storm. He has sold three magazine covers this year already. He is not getting a fourth.

d4.name: Supercell train
d4.desc: A first tornadic storm, then a second in its wake. The river cuts the map in two: the bridges are few.

d5.name: Dusk
d5.desc: The light is fading fast and the storm lights up with lightning. Callahan is here again. Lightning shots are worth gold tonight.

d6.name: Moderate risk
d6.desc: The Prediction Center has put the region under a moderate risk. Two likely tornadoes, one strong. Teo has serviced the probes.

d7.name: Mud
d7.desc: It rained all night: the dirt roads are skating rinks. Two cells, and Callahan who never lets go.

d8.name: High risk
d8.desc: The kind of day you see once a decade. A single monstrous supercell, three tornadoes forecast. Stay alive.

garage.title: THE GARAGE
garage.intro: Every dossier sold pays for fuel, repairs… and upgrades. Choose well.
garage.armor_desc: Less damage from hail and debris

ending.credits: TEMPÊTE — design, code, music: a one-person studio and a handful of skies. Thanks for chasing with us.

d1: Right. One isolated cell to the south-west, decent shear, a low enough base. Nothing historic, but it's a real storm.
Let's roll. Margot, camera ready? Teo, probes strapped down?
Always. I want its whole structure in the frame, from a distance, before the rain hides it.
Three turtles on the rack. If a tornado touches down, I want to be in front of it, not behind.
d2: Two cells today. The first one is already there, the second will form further north this afternoon.
Dry for now. Under the rain they will be mud: keep an eye on the pavement.
d3: Well, the truck. Going to photograph my rear bumper again?
Dutch Callahan. He poses in front of tornadoes for magazine covers.
Then we take the tornado from him. Before him, and better.
d4: A supercell train. The first is ready to produce, the second follows in its wake.
The river cuts the map. How many bridges?
Not enough. Look at them on the radar before you commit.
d5: Dusk and an electric storm. It's the kind of evening that makes a career.
I saved you a seat. At the back. Behind me.
d6: Moderate risk. Two likely tornadoes, and the second could be strong. We play it tight today.
I reinforced the probes. Put them on its path, I’ll handle the rest.
d7: It rained all night. The dirt roads are skating rinks.
Then we stay on pavement and plan ahead. Whoever gets stuck today goes home empty-handed.
d8: High risk. I've only seen this twice. A single supercell — but what a supercell.
The photo of the decade is somewhere in there.
And all four of us come home. That’s the only rule.

intro.text: The Great Plains, in spring. Every afternoon, the sky stacks itself into twenty-kilometre towers.
Some of them rotate. They are called supercells. A few give birth to a tornado.
June, Eli, Margot and Teo drive toward them in an armoured pick-up with three probes and a camera. For science, for the picture — and for that feeling.

finale.text: On June eleventh, under the high risk, the truck watched the season’s biggest tornado pass less than two kilometres away.
That evening, on the tailgate, nobody spoke for a long time. Then Margot brought out the prints.
The season is over. The sky will start again next year. So will they.
